final_goal: Reusable, provider-neutral story visual asset system that searches and reuses accepted assets, then uses reference-driven derive/edit before new image generation.

current_gate.next: Run G1A early-discrimination benchmark with low-quality-first screening: 5 tasks × 3 style profiles under controlled settings; record real usage/cost, retry rate, consistency and visual quality, then promote only finalists to higher-quality validation.

cost_truth.documented: No verified evidence that semantic art style alone lowers billed image-output tokens at fixed model/quality/size.
cost_truth.strategy: Reduce new generations/retries; use low-quality-first screening where acceptable; use direct reuse/reference-driven edit; exploit prompt caching where supported.

unknowns: Which of the three style candidates best clears the quality floor with the lowest retry/call burden.
Actual provider-specific billed usage/cost delta under controlled settings.
How well each style survives derive/edit while preserving character and environment continuity.
Minimum reusable asset set needed before reuse rate materially lowers new-generation demand.
Whether structured metadata remains sufficient after the library grows.
